1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	\paragraph{Multi-channel depth encoding.}
5	Four importance measures (Gini, SHAP, permutation, CPI; Kendall's $W{=}0.90$) converge on the same feature ranking, and Binoculars-derived features independently reach 78.1\%, not statistically distinguishable from 78.4\% (permutation $p{>}0.05$; merged: 82.6\%).
6	Depth signal is a distributional property encoded across multiple statistical channels; CORAL ordinal regression yields only marginal improvement (+0.3\,pp, Appendix~\ref{app:learned_estimator}), confirming ordinal structure is captured by the feature space rather than requiring specialized loss functions.
7	
8	\paragraph{Why neural methods underperform.}
9	End-to-end classifiers (DeBERTa, RoBERTa-DCOL) lag RF by 14--33\,pp (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}) despite full token-level context, confirming that depth is encoded in distributional tail statistics that pretrained representations do not capture (d2 recall as low as 8\%); targeted feature engineering is necessary, not merely convenient.
10	
11	\paragraph{Feature hierarchy across depths.}
12	The importance transition from \texttt{var\_surprisal} at shallow boundaries to perplexity tail statistics at deeper ones (\S\ref{sec:atlas:features}) mirrors tail-contraction dynamics: early recursion narrows the surprisal distribution while later steps erode the perplexity tail, consistent with geometric contraction (\S\ref{sec:method:theory}).
13	
14	\paragraph{Deployment considerations.}
15	The strategy effect (9.3\,pp) exceeding the model effect (7.2\,pp) requires auditing pipelines to condition on decoding configuration (\S\ref{sec:gen:crossstrategy}), echoing \citet{schaeffer2025}.
16	Similarly, the pipeline relies on a fixed reference model (12/19 features from reference perplexity), with cross-architecture alternatives degrading by 4--11\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}); accuracy attenuation at 14B (\S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}) may be partially recoverable via scale-matched references.
17	A self-reference probe at 7B (52.1\%, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$; Appendix~\ref{app:qwen7b_selfref}) falls 8\,pp below the cross-reference baseline (60.1\%), revealing a self-reference ceiling where d0/d1 become indistinguishable to the generator's own distribution; cross-model references may be necessary above ${\sim}$7B.
18	
19	\paragraph{Accumulation and outlook.}
20	Depth estimation bridges binary detection and model collapse research by providing ordinal resolution \cite{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse}.
21	Accumulation experiments at 25--50\% synthetic mixing (Appendix~\ref{app:accumulation_auc}) partially validate depth estimation under realistic conditions: $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ is preserved in 5/6 cells, with only GPT-2~XL d2-vs-d3 marginally below threshold (AUC\,=\,0.695 vs.\ $T{=}0.70$).
22	Cross-boundary chains (model A generates d1, model B generates d2, model C generates d3) maintain 84.8\% accuracy with reverse-chain confound control (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_boundary}), providing preliminary evidence that depth signal is process-level rather than generator-specific.
23	Extension to higher mixing ratios, cross-strategy accumulation, and frontier-scale models remains open.
24

1	\begin{abstract}
2	As language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises, yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
3	We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification and construct a benchmark of 180K cell-instances (140K unique passages) spanning three model families, three decoding strategies, and four depths under controlled full-replacement chains at the 1--1.5B parameter scale.
4	A lightweight pipeline (19 statistical features classified by Random Forest) achieves d1--d3 balanced accuracy of 59--82\% across nine model--strategy cells, with $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70} = 3$ in 8/9 cells.
5	Three findings emerge: (1)~depth signal concentrates in perplexity distribution tails, corroborated by classifier convergence and independent cross-perplexity features; (2)~decoding strategy affects cross-condition transfer more than model architecture, suggesting structurally distinct degradation trajectories; (3)~signal attenuates with scale (14B cross-reference accuracy ${\sim}44$\%, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$ for nucleus and temperature, 0 for top-$k$), with reference-model choice accounting for ${\sim}7$\,pp of the apparent degradation.
6	Our depth estimation claims hold most strongly within-strategy or when the decoding configuration is known; a two-stage routing pipeline recovers $+$11.5\,pp under cross-strategy transfer.
7	Perturbation-based and membership-inference baselines lack ordinal depth resolution, confirming that depth estimation requires distributional statistics beyond binary detection scores.
8	\end{abstract}

\begin{abstract}
As language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises, yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification and construct a benchmark of 180K cell-instances (140K unique passages) spanning three model families, three decoding strategies, and four depths under controlled full-replacement chains at the 1--1.5B parameter scale.
A lightweight pipeline (19 statistical features classified by Random Forest) achieves d1--d3 balanced accuracy of 59--82\% across nine model--strategy cells, with $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70} = 3$ in 8/9 cells.
Three findings emerge: (1)~depth signal concentrates in perplexity distribution tails, corroborated by classifier convergence and independent cross-perplexity features; (2)~decoding strategy affects cross-condition transfer more than model architecture, suggesting structurally distinct degradation trajectories; (3)~signal attenuates with scale (14B cross-reference accuracy ${\sim}44$\%, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$ for nucleus and temperature, 0 for top-$k$), with reference-model choice accounting for ${\sim}7$\,pp of the apparent degradation.
Our depth estimation claims hold most strongly within-strategy or when the decoding configuration is known; a two-stage routing pipeline recovers $+$11.5\,pp under cross-strategy transfer.
Perturbation-based and membership-inference baselines lack ordinal depth resolution, confirming that depth estimation requires distributional statistics beyond binary detection scores.
\end{abstract}

33	\paragraph{Generation pipeline.}
34	Starting from a Wikipedia subset ($\mathcal{D}_0$), each cycle: (1)~LoRA finetuning \cite{hu2022lora} on $\mathcal{D}_{k-1}$ ($r{=}16$, $\alpha{=}32$, lr $2{\times}10^{-4}$, effective batch 16, 3 epochs, dropout $0.05$; fresh adapter from the base model at each depth; full protocol in Appendix~\ref{app:lora_protocol}); (2)~sampling 5{,}000 passages (max 512 tokens, beginning-of-sequence (BOS) seeded) under the specified strategy; (3)~$\mathcal{D}_k$ feeds the next cycle.
35	Each depth is produced by a model trained on prior-depth data, not by sampling from the unmodified base model.
36	BOS seeding may amplify depth signal; prompted-generation validation (Appendix~\ref{app:prompted_gen}) confirms signal persistence albeit attenuated ($-$13.8\,pp).
37	No per-passage lineage exists across depths; cross-validation splits do not introduce leakage.

41	This overlaps with one generator (Pythia), conferring a 4--11\,pp self-reference advantage on that pipeline (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}); Pythia results in Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} are marked $^\dagger$ accordingly.

44	\subsection{Statistical Feature Design}
45	\label{sec:method:features}
46	
47	We extract a feature vector $\mathbf{f}(x)$ comprising 19 candidate features from the reference-model perplexity distribution over each passage $x$; ablation (\S\ref{sec:atlas:features}) shows the top 5 achieve 97.6\% of full-set performance, and variance inflation analysis reveals VIF${>}$10 for 14--16 features; effective independent dimensionality is ${\approx}$4--5.

51	\centering
52	\small

54	\label{tab:features}

56	\toprule
57	Category & Features & $n$ \\
58	\midrule
59	Perplexity & mean, var, skewness, kurtosis, & 9 \\

73	\emph{Perplexity statistics} (9 features) capture the per-token perplexity distribution via moments and quantiles (p10--p90); tail quantiles are especially informative as recursive finetuning erodes the high-perplexity tail (\S\ref{sec:atlas}).
74	\emph{Surprisal statistics} (3 features): mean, variance, and entropy of $-\log p(\text{token})$.
75	\emph{Lexical diversity} (4 features): type--token ratio, hapax ratio, bigram/trigram entropy.

78	\subsection{Effective Discriminable Depth}
79	\label{sec:method:edd}
80	
81	Aggregate multi-class accuracy obscures whether discriminability degrades at specific depth boundaries.
82	We propose the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) as an operational measure of how far into a recursive chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable.
83	
84	\paragraph{Pairwise discriminability.}
85	Let $\mathcal{D} = \{0, 1, \dots, K\}$ denote the depth set and $T \in (0.5, 1.0]$ a discrimination threshold.
86	For each adjacent pair $(d, d{+}1)$, we define the pairwise discriminability $\mathrm{AUC}(d, d{+}1)$ as the area under the ROC curve of a dedicated binary Random Forest classifier (500 trees, $\lfloor\sqrt{19}\rfloor$ candidate features per split) trained on class-balanced data from $\mathbf{f}(x)$ (\S\ref{sec:method:features}) to distinguish depth-$d$ from depth-$(d{+}1)$ samples, evaluated via 5-fold stratified cross-validation.
87	Each pair uses an independent classifier to avoid decision boundary dilution from multi-class settings.
88	
89	\begin{definition}[Effective Discriminable Depth]
90	\label{def:edd}
91	The \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} at threshold $T$ is:
92	\begin{multline}
93	\mathrm{EDD}_T = \max \bigl\{ d^*{+}1 \,:\, \\
94	\forall\, d' \leq d^*,\; \mathrm{AUC}(d', d'{+}1) \geq T \bigr\}
95	\label{eq:edd}
96	\end{multline}
97	where $d^* \in \{0, \dots, K{-}1\}$. If\, $\mathrm{AUC}(0,1) < T$, then $\mathrm{EDD}_T = 0$.
98	\end{definition}
99	
100	$\mathrm{EDD}_T$ reports the longest \emph{contiguous} discriminable prefix: the deepest $d$ such that every pair from $(0,1)$ through $(d{-}1, d)$ exceeds $T$.
101	All AUC profiles in the primary benchmark decay monotonically; non-monotonic profiles occur only in cross-scale extensions (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}).
102	We adopt $T{=}0.70$ following the ``acceptable discrimination'' threshold in ROC analysis \cite{hosmer2000} (8/9 cells achieve $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70} \geq 3$); sensitivity analysis (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}) shows $\mathrm{EDD}$ shifts by at most one level across $T \in \{0.65, 0.70, 0.80\}$ in all nine cells.
103	
104	\paragraph{Classifiers.}
105	Our primary classifier is a Random Forest (200 trees, unconstrained depth, 5-fold CV; EDD binary classifiers use 500 trees).\footnote{Statistical tests are not corrected for multiple comparisons; $p$-values should be interpreted as exploratory.}
106	The RF produces ordinally consistent predictions: 98.2\% of errors fall on adjacent depths ($|\Delta| \leq 1$), quadratic weighted kappa (QWK)\,=\,0.89.
107	Comparisons against other classifiers and detection baselines appear in \S\ref{sec:generalization}.

1	\subsection{Theoretical Motivation}
2	\label{sec:method:theory}
3	
4	Recursive generation contracts the support of the learned distribution, with low-probability tokens lost first \cite{shumailov2024_nature}: tail mass $P_k(\mathrm{ppl} > t)$ decreases monotonically in depth $k$.
5	This tail erosion predicts the perplexity tail feature family as a depth marker, confirmed jointly with surprisal variance across all 9 cells (\S\ref{sec:atlas:features}).
6	Surprisal variance captures complementary distributional narrowing: as the support contracts, per-token surprise becomes more predictable.
7	
8	\paragraph{EDD upper bound.}
9	Tail mass at depth $k$ scales as $\alpha^k$ for a contraction factor $\alpha \in (0,1)$ \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}; EDD reaches its upper bound when adjacent-depth feature distance falls below classifier resolution.
10	Our empirical AUC-excess contraction (ratio 0.80 at d1v2$\to$d2v3, 0.69 at d3v4$\to$d4v5; \S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}) is consistent with geometric decay approaching a fixed point \cite{bertrand2024_stability}.
11	5-class extensions to d4 (71--80\%, chance = 20\%; Appendix~\ref{app:depth4_ext}) confirm depth~4 discriminability; mean perplexity saturates before tail statistics, placing a physical ceiling on EDD.
12	
13	\paragraph{Scale-dependent attenuation.}
14	Larger models approximate the training distribution more faithfully per step ($\alpha$ closer to 1), predicting weaker per-step signal.
15	Qwen2.5-14B supports this: d0-vs-d1 AUC drops to 0.643 (vs.\ ${>}0.99$ at 1--1.5B; \S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}); 7--8B results are mixed, suggesting additional confounds interact with the scale effect (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}).
16	
17	\paragraph{Strategy-dependent convergence.}
18	The contraction rate $\alpha$ varies with decoding strategy.
19	Temperature scaling ($\tau < 1$) sharpens the logit distribution uniformly and accelerates convergence to the mode; temperature depth-$d$ text should therefore resemble nucleus depth-$(d{+}1)$ text in tail statistics.
20	GPT-2~XL confirms this: temperature d1 median \texttt{p90\_ppl} (92.2) matches the nucleus d2 median (92.3).
21	Top-$k$ truncation removes the low-probability tokens that carry depth signal, predicting weaker discriminability; top-$k$ cells yield the lowest accuracy (68.9--75.8\%) across the atlas (\S\ref{sec:atlas:strategy}).

\subsection{Theoretical Motivation}
\label{sec:method:theory}

Recursive generation contracts the support of the learned distribution, with low-probability tokens lost first \cite{shumailov2024_nature}: tail mass $P_k(\mathrm{ppl} > t)$ decreases monotonically in depth $k$.
This tail erosion predicts the perplexity tail feature family as a depth marker, confirmed jointly with surprisal variance across all 9 cells (\S\ref{sec:atlas:features}).
Surprisal variance captures complementary distributional narrowing: as the support contracts, per-token surprise becomes more predictable.

\paragraph{EDD upper bound.}
Tail mass at depth $k$ scales as $\alpha^k$ for a contraction factor $\alpha \in (0,1)$ \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}; EDD reaches its upper bound when adjacent-depth feature distance falls below classifier resolution.
Our empirical AUC-excess contraction (ratio 0.80 at d1v2$\to$d2v3, 0.69 at d3v4$\to$d4v5; \S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}) is consistent with geometric decay approaching a fixed point \cite{bertrand2024_stability}.
5-class extensions to d4 (71--80\%, chance = 20\%; Appendix~\ref{app:depth4_ext}) confirm depth~4 discriminability; mean perplexity saturates before tail statistics, placing a physical ceiling on EDD.

\paragraph{Scale-dependent attenuation.}
Larger models approximate the training distribution more faithfully per step ($\alpha$ closer to 1), predicting weaker per-step signal.
Qwen2.5-14B supports this: d0-vs-d1 AUC drops to 0.643 (vs.\ ${>}0.99$ at 1--1.5B; \S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}); 7--8B results are mixed, suggesting additional confounds interact with the scale effect (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}).

\paragraph{Strategy-dependent convergence.}
The contraction rate $\alpha$ varies with decoding strategy.
Temperature scaling ($\tau < 1$) sharpens the logit distribution uniformly and accelerates convergence to the mode; temperature depth-$d$ text should therefore resemble nucleus depth-$(d{+}1)$ text in tail statistics.
GPT-2~XL confirms this: temperature d1 median \texttt{p90\_ppl} (92.2) matches the nucleus d2 median (92.3).
Top-$k$ truncation removes the low-probability tokens that carry depth signal, predicting weaker discriminability; top-$k$ cells yield the lowest accuracy (68.9--75.8\%) across the atlas (\S\ref{sec:atlas:strategy}).

## Simulated EMNLP 2026 ARR Review

### Paper Summary
The paper formalizes "recursive generation depth estimation" — given a text passage, determine how many times it has been through a model→data→model cycle (d0=human, d1-d3=synthetic). They construct a 180K-instance benchmark at 1-1.5B scale (3 models × 3 decoding strategies × 4 depths), extract 19 statistical features from a reference model, and classify with Random Forest. 

The main findings show 78.4% mean 4-class accuracy with an expected depth distance of 3 in 8 out of 9 test cells. They evaluate robustness across eight different generalization axes including cross-model, cross-strategy, cross-scale, and accumulation effects.

### Overall Assessment

Let me think about this carefully.

**Strengths:**
1. Genuinely novel task formalization. I've surveyed the field and no one has done ordinal depth estimation. This is a real gap.
2. Systematic benchmark with good coverage (3×3×4 grid).
3. EDD metric is a useful contribution to the field.
4. Thorough generalization testing (8 axes).
5.

The paper honestly reports negative results—cross-strategy performance drops to 45.9%, the 7B model hits a self-reference ceiling at 52%, and neural methods underperform expectations. The Binoculars convergence finding (78.1% ≈ 78.4%) provides independent validation of the results. The cross-boundary chain experiment with reverse-chain control is well-designed.

**Weaknesses:**
1. **Scale**: 1-1.5B models aren't frontier, and the 14B results (44-51%) reveal significant scaling challenges. The 7B self-reference ceiling further constrains practical applicability, which the paper acknowledges but the gap remains substantial.

2. **Full-replacement chains are artificial**: Real contamination involves partial mixing and diverse sources, not just complete replacement. The accumulation experiments (25-50% mixing) partially address this, though only two mixing ratios were tested and full-replacement remains the primary benchmark.

3. **Methodological novelty**: Random forests on hand-crafted features isn't particularly novel—the paper frames this as "task formalization + empirical characterization," which is reasonable, but the method is straightforward: compute perplexity statistics and train a classifier. There's also a notable 13.8 percentage point gap between BOS-seeded and prompted generation that affects the results.

4. **Reference model dependency**: Twelve of nineteen features require a fixed reference model, creating a hard operational constraint. ## 模拟 EMNLP 2026 ARR 审稿

---

### 1. Overall Assessment: **3.0 (Findings)**

**Summary**: 论文形式化了一个真正新颖的任务（递归生成深度估计），构建了系统性的 benchmark，并通过 8 个泛化维度进行了彻底的实证分析。任务定义清晰，EDD 指标有用，negative results 诚实报告。但 1-1.5B 尺度限制了实际影响力，full-replacement 设定人工化，方法论（RF on 19 features）缺乏创新。适合 Findings，不足以进入 Conference。

---

### 2. 最可能拒稿的 3 个理由

**理由 1（最严重）: Scale relevance — 1-1.5B 模型实用价值有限**

问题描述：论文的核心 claims 全部基于 1-1.5B 参数模型。7B self-reference 仅 52.1%（2.1× chance），14B cross-reference 44.1%。在 frontier models（70B+）主导实际生成的今天，1-1.5B 的结果能否 generalize 完全未知。

审稿人可能措辞：*"The paper's strongest results are limited to the 1-1.5B regime. At 7B, self-reference accuracy barely exceeds 2× chance and EDD drops to 0 — the method cannot distinguish d0 from d1 using the generator's own distribution. Given that practical recursive contamination involves 7B+ models, the paper's findings, while interesting as a proof-of-concept, have limited applicability. The self-reference ceiling (Discussion §5) actually undermines the paper's premise: if larger models assign similar probabilities to d0 and d1 text, the depth signal that the paper relies on may simply not exist at frontier scale."*

当前 defense：
- Abstract L3: "at the 1--1.5B parameter scale" — 明确 scope limiting ✓
- Intro L7: "We focus on the 1--1.5B parameter regime" ✓
- §4.4: 14B 结果标记为 "Preliminary Cross-Scale Observations" ✓
- Discussion L17: self-reference ceiling 诚实报告 ✓
- Theory §2.3: "Larger models approximate the training distribution more faithfully per step" 提供理论解释 ✓

**Defense 强度: adequate.** 论文诚实限定了 scope，但审稿人的 concern 不是 "你有没有承认"，而是 "这个结果有没有意义"。在 1-1.5B 能做但在 7B+ 不能做的方法，其科学贡献取决于你是否相信理论框架会推广——而 7B/14B 的经验数据恰恰显示它不推广。

---

**理由 2: Ecological validity — full-replacement + BOS seeding 过于人工化**

问题描述：primary benchmark 使用 full-replacement chains（每次完全替换训练集）+ BOS-seeded generation（无 prompt），这两者都是极端设定。真实 web 污染是 partial accumulation + prompted/instruction-following generation。

审稿人可能措辞：*"The full-replacement protocol isolates the depth variable cleanly, but this isolation comes at the cost of ecological validity. In practice, (1) contamination is partial — a model might see 5-10% synthetic text, not 100%; (2) generation is prompted, not BOS-seeded — the 13.8pp gap between BOS and prompted generation (Appendix B.18) suggests the depth signal is partly an artifact of unconditional generation; (3) training involves diverse corpora, not a single Wikipedia seed. The accumulation experiments (25-50% mixing) are helpful but test only two mixing ratios and three of nine cells. The authors frame full-replacement as an 'upper bound on signal strength,' but this framing is unfalsifiable — we cannot know if the signal mechanism is the same under realistic conditions."*

当前 defense：
- Intro L7: "full replacement provides an upper bound on depth signal strength" ✓
- Accumulation (Appendix + Discussion L21): EDD=3 preserved in 5/6 cells at 25-50% mixing ✓
- Prompted-gen validation (Appendix + Limitations L12): signal persists but -13.8pp ✓
- Cross-domain arXiv (§4.4): 74.1% ✓

**Defense 强度: adequate but not strong.** "Upper bound" framing 合理但不够——审稿人想看的是 "real-world performance"，而 accumulation 只测了 2 个 mixing ratio、3 个 cell。BOS-vs-prompted 的 13.8pp gap 被诚实报告但实际上是一个严重的 concern：如果去掉 BOS artifact，main benchmark 的 78.4% 可能降到 ~65%。

---

**理由 3: 联合条件限制 — 需同时知道 reference model + decoding strategy**

问题描述：pipeline 需要 (a) 固定的 reference model（12/19 features 来自 reference perplexity），(b) 已知的 decoding strategy（cross-strategy transfer 45.9%，仅 1.4× chance for d1-d3）。在实际部署中两者都未知。

审稿人可能措辞：*"The pipeline's deployment assumptions are prohibitively strong. The user must know which reference model to use (cross-architecture degradation of 4-11pp) AND which decoding strategy the text was generated with (cross-strategy d1-d3 balanced accuracy of 45.9%, barely above the 33% chance baseline). The two-stage pipeline recovers to 70.5%, but this requires training an additional strategy classifier with access to strategy-labeled data — a circular requirement. In realistic deployment scenarios where neither the generator model nor the decoding strategy is known, the method's claimed accuracy drops from 78.4% to somewhere in the 46-67% range, substantially weakening the practical contribution."*

当前 defense：
- Discussion ¶4 L15: strategy effect > model effect 如实报告 ✓
- §4.3: two-stage pipeline +11.5pp recovery ✓
- §4.2: cross-model transfer 66.4% 仍 2.7× chance ✓
- Discussion L22: cross-boundary chains 84.8% ✓

**Defense 强度: weak.** 论文承认了问题但没有解决。cross-strategy 45.9% 是整篇论文最大的软肋——它意味着在最现实的部署场景（strategy 未知）下，d1-d3 深度估计几乎是随机的。two-stage pipeline 需要 strategy labels，这在 wild 场景中不可得。cross-model transfer (66.4%) 好得多但仍是 nucleus-only。

---

### 3. 最薄弱的 Claim

**Contribution 3: "Accumulation robustness"**

4 个 core claims：
1. Task formalization + EDD + benchmark — **strong**（无人做过，25 篇 survey 确认 gap）
2. Depth Degradation Atlas — **strong**（9 cells, 4 importance measures, feature ablation）
3. Accumulation robustness — **weakest** ⬇️
4. Generalization boundaries — **adequate**（"boundaries" 本身就是限定性表述）

Contribution 3 是最薄弱的，原因：

**(a) "Robustness" 一词过度承诺。** 8-15pp accuracy attenuation 不是 robust——那是显著退化。论文说 "EDD=3 preserved in 5/6 cells"，但：
- 1/6 failure = 17% failure rate on 仅 6 个样本
- GPT-2 XL d2v3 AUC = 0.695，离 T=0.70 仅差 0.005——阈值微调即可翻转 claim
- "Despite -8-15pp accuracy attenuation" 中的 "despite" 做了大量 rhetorical work

**(b) 覆盖不足。** 只测了 3 cells（GPT-2 XL nucleus, Pythia nucleus, OLMo temp）× 2 mixing ratios (25%, 50%)。没有 cross-strategy accumulation，没有 5%/10% 低 mixing ratio（更接近真实场景），没有不同 seed。

**(c) 与 contribution 标题不匹配。** 标题写 "robustness"，但数据展示的是 "the method still works but significantly worse under partial mixing"。这是 "graceful degradation"，不是 "robustness"。

**修复建议**：将 contribution 3 从 "Accumulation robustness" 改为 "Accumulation characterization" 或 "Partial accumulation validation"，并在正文中用 "partial validation" 而非 "robustness"。这不会减弱 claim（数据没变），但会防止审稿人攻击措辞过强。

---

### 4. FPR 15-34% 更新后的 framing 一致性

**更新不影响 Discussion 的 deployment narrative。** 当前状态：
- FPR 仅出现在 Limitations L13："raw false-positive rates reach 15--34%, reducible to below 7%"
- Discussion ¶4 ("Deployment considerations") 讨论了 strategy effect、reference model、self-reference ceiling，但**完全没提 FPR**
- Abstract 和 Intro 均未提 FPR

**这个遗漏本身是一个问题。** Discussion ¶4 名为 "Deployment considerations" 却遗漏了最重要的部署指标——在真实 web 数据上 15-34% 的误报率。审稿人会认为作者在回避这个问题。

**建议**：在 Discussion ¶4 末尾（L17 之后）加 1 句：
*"On held-out web-crawl corpora, raw false-positive rates reach 15--34\% but are reducible to below 7\% via posterior-threshold calibration (Limitations)."*

这将 FPR 从 "隐藏在 Limitations 中的弱点" 转为 "在 Discussion 中主动 address 的挑战"，符合同领域论文的做法（如 Binoculars 在主文中讨论 FPR）。

---

### 5. 如果只能改一处来提分

**将 Discussion ¶4 的 "Deployment considerations" 扩展为 "Deployment: capabilities and constraints"，加入 FPR threshold calibration + cross-boundary chain 两个 defense point。**

当前 Discussion ¶4 只列问题（strategy effect、reference dependency、self-reference ceiling），读起来像 Limitations 的延伸。审稿人看完会觉得 "这个方法在部署中完全不可行"。

加 2 句话（不影响页数）：
1. FPR threshold calibration（从 Limitations 提升到 Discussion level）
2. Cross-boundary chains 84.8%（已在 ¶5 L22，可在 ¶4 交叉引用）

这样 ¶4 的叙事变为："部署有这些挑战（strategy/reference/scale），但也有这些解决路径（threshold calibration/two-stage routing/cross-model reference），且 depth signal 是 process-level 的（cross-boundary 84.8%）。"

**预期影响**：从 3.0 → 3.0-3.2。不会突破 3.5（那需要 scale experiments），但把 "purely limitation-focused deployment paragraph" 转为 "challenges AND partial solutions" 是 Findings 评审中最有效的 framing 调整。

\subsection{Theoretical Motivation}
\label{sec:method:theory}

Recursive generation contracts the support of the learned distribution, with low-probability tokens lost first \cite{shumailov2024_nature}: tail mass $P_k(\mathrm{ppl} > t)$ decreases monotonically in depth $k$.
This tail erosion predicts the perplexity tail feature family as a depth marker, confirmed jointly with surprisal variance across all 9 cells (\S\ref{sec:atlas:features}).
Surprisal variance captures complementary distributional narrowing: as the support contracts, per-token surprise becomes more predictable.

\paragraph{EDD upper bound.}
Tail mass at depth $k$ scales as $\alpha^k$ for a contraction factor $\alpha \in (0,1)$ \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}; EDD reaches its upper bound when adjacent-depth feature distance falls below classifier resolution.
Our empirical AUC-excess contraction (ratio 0.80 at d1v2$\to$d2v3, 0.69 at d3v4$\to$d4v5; \S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}) is consistent with geometric decay approaching a fixed point \cite{bertrand2024_stability}.
5-class extensions to d4 (71--81\%, chance = 20\%; Appendix~\ref{app:depth4_ext}) confirm depth~4 discriminability; mean perplexity saturates before tail statistics, placing a physical ceiling on EDD.

\paragraph{Scale-dependent attenuation.}
Larger models approximate the training distribution more faithfully per step ($\alpha$ closer to 1), predicting weaker per-step signal.
Qwen2.5-14B supports this: d0-vs-d1 AUC drops to 0.643 (vs.\ ${>}0.98$ at 1--1.5B; \S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}); 7--8B results are mixed, suggesting additional confounds interact with the scale effect (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}).

\paragraph{Strategy-dependent convergence.}
The contraction rate $\alpha$ varies with decoding strategy.
Temperature scaling ($\tau < 1$) sharpens the logit distribution uniformly and accelerates convergence to the mode; temperature depth-$d$ text should therefore resemble nucleus depth-$(d{+}1)$ text in tail statistics.
GPT-2~XL confirms this: temperature d1 median \texttt{p90\_ppl} (92.2) matches the nucleus d2 median (92.3).
Top-$k$ truncation removes the low-probability tokens that carry depth signal, predicting weaker discriminability; top-$k$ cells yield the lowest accuracy (68.9--75.8\%) across the atlas (\S\ref{sec:atlas:strategy}).

\begin{abstract}
As language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises, yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification and construct a benchmark of 180K cell-instances (140K unique passages) spanning three model families, three decoding strategies, and four depths under controlled full-replacement chains at the 1--1.5B parameter scale.
A lightweight pipeline (19 statistical features classified by Random Forest) achieves d1--d3 balanced accuracy of 59--82\% across nine model--strategy cells, with $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70} = 3$ in 8/9 cells.
Three findings emerge: (1)~depth signal concentrates in perplexity distribution tails, corroborated by classifier convergence and independent cross-perplexity features; (2)~decoding strategy affects cross-condition transfer more than model architecture, suggesting structurally distinct degradation trajectories; (3)~signal attenuates with scale (14B cross-reference accuracy ${\sim}44$\%, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$ for nucleus and temperature, 0 for top-$k$), with reference-model choice shifting accuracy by ${\sim}7$\,pp and altering EDD, indicating it is a major confound in cross-scale comparisons.
Our depth estimation claims hold most strongly within-strategy or when the decoding configuration is known; a two-stage routing pipeline recovers $+$11.5\,pp under cross-strategy transfer.
Perturbation-based and membership-inference baselines lack ordinal depth resolution, confirming that depth estimation requires distributional statistics beyond binary detection scores.
\end{abstract}

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

Four importance measures converge on the same feature ranking (Kendall's $W{=}0.90$); Binoculars-derived features independently reach 78.1\%, not statistically distinguishable from 78.4\% (merged: 82.6\%).
CORAL ordinal regression yields only +0.3\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:learned_estimator}), confirming ordinal structure is captured by the feature space.
End-to-end classifiers lag RF by 14--33\,pp (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}) despite full token-level context (d2 F1 ${\leq}$0.26; Appendix~\ref{app:e2e}), confirming that targeted feature engineering is necessary.
The strategy effect (9.3\,pp) exceeding the model effect (7.2\,pp) requires conditioning on decoding configuration (\S\ref{sec:gen:crossstrategy}).
The pipeline relies on a fixed reference model; cross-architecture alternatives degrade by 4--11\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}), and a 7B self-reference probe ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$; Appendix~\ref{app:qwen7b_selfref}) reveals a self-reference ceiling.
Accumulation experiments and cross-boundary chains (84.8\%; Appendix~\ref{app:accumulation_auc},~\ref{app:cross_boundary}) suggest depth signal is process-level.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

The text on which large language models are trained increasingly contains their own outputs.
As synthetic content proliferates across the web, a recursive loop emerges: models trained on web corpora ingest text generated by earlier models, and their outputs feed into the next generation's training data \cite{shumailov2024_nature,alemohammad2024_mad}.
This model$\to$data$\to$model cycle is no longer hypothetical; it is already occurring in the wild. Yet whether the recursive generation depth of a text can be estimated from its statistical properties remains unstudied, a question that matters because first-generation synthetic text may be benign or even beneficial for training, while deeply recursive text drives the distributional collapse that degrades model quality \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}.
We focus on the 1--1.5B parameter regime under \emph{controlled full-replacement chains}, where each generation fully replaces the prior training set, isolating the depth variable. Real-world contamination involves partial mixing at unknown proportions; full replacement provides an upper bound on depth signal strength (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

Existing tools address adjacent but distinct problems.
Binary detectors \cite{binoculars2024,fast_detectgpt2024,diveye2026} collapse all depths $d \geq 1$ into a single category, a limitation we confirm empirically: their pairwise d1-vs-d2 AUC collapses to chance level (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}); watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} requires proactive embedding.
The model collapse literature \cite{shumailov2024_nature,dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails} assumes depth is known a priori; \citet{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse} filter synthetic data via binary detection without distinguishing depths.
No existing method estimates the ordinal recursive generation depth of a text passage from its content alone (Figure~\ref{fig:problem}).

We find that recursive generation leaves quantifiable statistical fingerprints in text, and these fingerprints are \textbf{consistent in direction but scale-dependent in magnitude} across the three model families and three decoding strategies studied.
Specifically, the perplexity tail feature family (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) and surprisal variance emerge as dominant depth indicators, with group-level dominance robust across all 9 model--strategy configurations and three importance measures.
Our contribution centers on task formalization and systematic empirical characterization; the convergence of four classifiers within 0.8\,pp (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}) confirms that signal resides in feature design, not classifier architecture.
We formalize recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification and find that a lightweight pipeline suffices: compute 19 reference-model statistical features (effective dimensionality ${\approx}$4--5 due to multicollinearity; \S\ref{sec:atlas:features}) and classify with a Random Forest into $K{+}1$ depth classes.
To characterize how recursive generation reshapes these features, we construct the \emph{Depth Degradation Atlas}: a $3 \times 3$ grid of model families $\times$ decoding strategies spanning 4 depths (180K cell-instances).
The atlas reveals strategy-dependent degradation trajectories; we introduce \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) to quantify how far into the recursion chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.68\textwidth]{figures/fig_problem_illustration.pdf}
\caption{Recursive generation depth estimation. A seed corpus $\mathcal{D}_0$ feeds a LoRA finetuning--sampling loop producing successively deeper corpora. Given a passage~$x$, the task is to estimate its ordinal depth~$d$.}
\label{fig:problem}
\end{figure*}
Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Task formalization and metric.} We define recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification, introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric, and construct a 180K cell-instance benchmark ($3$ model families $\times$ $3$ decoding strategies $\times$ $4$ depths; 140K unique passages).

    \item \textbf{Depth Degradation Atlas.} The perplexity tail feature family and surprisal variance jointly dominate depth discrimination across all 9 cells; $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ in 8/9 cells (4 under nucleus depth extension), validated by 5-class extension (71--81\%); feature group ablation confirms perplexity tail dominance (76.6\% alone vs.\ 78.4\% full set).

    \item \textbf{Partial-mixing validation.} Under 25--50\% synthetic mixing, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ is preserved in 5/6 cells with $-$8--15\,pp accuracy attenuation.

    \item \textbf{Generalization boundaries.} Within the tested 1--1.5B regime, cross-model transfer reaches 66.4\% and cross-domain (arXiv) 74.1\%; at 14B, cross-reference $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$; cross-strategy (d1--d3: 45.9\%) is a boundary condition, partially recovered by two-stage routing ($+$11.5\,pp).
\end{itemize}
